data.title: Singapore's Manufacturing Growth Likely to Moderate in 2027 — Market Talk
data.description: Singapore's manufacturing growth is likely to moderate in 2027 from this year's strong momentum, CGS International economists say in a note. Industrial production growth accelerated in October, driven by strong performance in the precision engineering segment. Ongoing artificial intelligence infrastructure investment and semiconductor demand should support electronics production, they note. However, the potential moderation in next year's factory output would reflect a normalization in global electronics demand and a higher base, they say. CGS International projects Singapore's manufacturing growth to cool to 7.0% in 2027 from its 2026 forecast of 10.0%.(amanda.lee@wsj.com)

data.title: Key Clues About US MATCH Act Likely to Come From Defense Bill — Market Talk
data.description: Next week could be an important window to watch for clues as to whether the MATCH Act, which restricts semiconductor equipment and components exports to China, will be enacted soon, Bernstein analysts say in a note. The most prominent restriction under the Act could be of immersion DUV lithography tools from ASML and Nikon, which are essential for all advanced logic and memory chips, they note. "If enacted, it would impede China's ambition to expand capacity and impact all equipment companies' sales to China, not just ASML," they say. The biggest signal watch would be whether the final 2027 annual defense bill, likely released early December, includes the MATCH Act, Bernstein says.(sherry.qin@wsj.com)

data.title: Spotlighting Trends in Chinese-Language Music: TME Uni Chart Is Now on JOOX
data.description:
BEIJING, Nov. 27, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- TME Uni Chart has officially launched on JOOX, the international music streaming platform under Tencent Music Entertainment Group (TME). Music fans across the globe can now view and engage with the full chart on JOOX, stream hit tracks, and support their favourite artists and songs.

As one of the flagship chart products under the authoritative TME Chart, TME Uni Chart adheres to the mission of "Charting Real Popularity Through Data". Drawing on authentic user‑behaviour data across multiple platforms, it calculates track performance based on three core dimensions: streaming popularity, sales performance and recommendation index. A comprehensive set of metrics including streams, favourites and shares are incorporated, alongside robust anti‑manipulation validation mechanisms. Widely recognised within the industry as a credible benchmark for measuring mainstream reception of new Chinese‑language releases, the chart documents shifting trends across the Chinese‑language music scene and delivers reliable market‑heat insights for musicians, record labels, brands and music audiences.

As TME's overseas streaming hub, JOOX has built a strong presence across Hong Kong SAR, Macao SAR, Thailand, Malaysia, Indonesia and other markets. Boasting a massive global music library, sophisticated localised operations and a well‑developed fan‑interaction ecosystem, JOOX delivers fresh, trendy and diverse music content to young audiences in different regions, and has built a substantial regional user base. With deep insights into Southeast Asian listeners' musical tastes, JOOX serves as a key gateway for Chinese‑language music to reach young overseas audiences, featuring strong capabilities in localised content distribution and social‑driven music discovery.

User streaming and engagement data generated on JOOX has long been factored into TME Uni Chart's calculation system. The official roll‑out of TME Uni Chart on JOOX brings dual value: overseas fans can keep up‑to‑date with new Chinese‑language music trends and gain greater exposure to Chinese‑language artists and their latest works, breaking down geographical barriers for Chinese‑language music. In addition, overseas users can directly take part in TME Uni Chart voting‑related campaigns within JOOX, enabling domestically‑popular releases to gain further traction and momentum in international markets.

Moving forward, TME Uni Chart will work hand‑in‑hand with JOOX to discover high‑quality Chinese‑language music productions, support Chinese‑language music in reaching broader global audiences, and allow music fans at home and abroad to experience the charm of Chinese‑language pop music together.

SOURCE Tencent Music Entertainment Group

data.title: The AI Boom Looks Alive and Well in Asia — WSJ
data.description:
By Jason Douglas

TOKYO — Panic and euphoria swept global stock markets as the Jensen Huang drama unfolded, showing just how angsty investors have become over the durability of the artificial-intelligence boom.

Dig into the economic data coming out of Asia, however, and for now at least the economic burst from the technology is still going strong, even as worries deepen about the risk of a pullback and how bad an AI slump could get.

The U.S. economy is also still feeling the AI wind in its sails. Revised figures showed the economy grew at an inflation-adjusted, annual rate of 4.3% in the third quarter, faster than the 3.4% first reported. Investment in nonresidential buildings, which includes data centers, grew at a 16% rate.

The data-center build-out in the U.S. and around the world leans heavily on exports of Taiwanese semiconductors, South Korean memory chips and high-tech equipment from countries including China, Japan and Singapore.

Export data give little indication that demand for these AI-linked products is slowing. If anything, order books suggest demand is still accelerating, especially for top-of-the-range chips such as those created by Nvidia.

"The data is still extraordinarily strong, particularly for Taiwan," said Paul Cavey, who runs East Asia Econ, a consulting firm that provides data and analysis on the region's economies.

The big beneficiaries of the export bonanza are the chip makers that manufacture the product at the center of the AI boom. Bumper profits at South Korea's Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix, as well as Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co., show the critical role these companies play in bringing Silicon Valley's AI dreams to life.

Growth in export earnings reflects not just a sharp rise in shipments of semiconductors and other components but a steep run-up in their price as demand spiraled.

Some economists say the recent leveling off in chip prices is an early sign the AI boom could be cresting. The worry for economists and institutions such as the International Monetary Fund is that Asia and the global economy more broadly are becoming too reliant on the AI industry to drive growth. That could leave the world vulnerable if and when the investment frenzy loses steam.

Asian economies aren't just exporting the essential components of data centers to the U.S. and elsewhere. Increasingly, they are turning into data-center hubs themselves. That is especially true in Southeast Asia, where data centers are springing up in countries including Malaysia and Thailand.

That trend could soon be over, however, as the U.S. seeks to block Chinese AI labs from accessing U.S. computing power overseas. Nvidia ordered partners in the region to pause shipments to Malaysia, Thailand, Singapore and Indonesia. The U.S. also tightened export rules to throttle Chinese access to the most advanced chips. A pullback in data-center construction would kick away a key engine of regional growth.

Asian markets have been on a stomach-churning ride this year as AI's fortunes have ebbed and flowed. The excitement has pulled in new investors and stoked stock-picking fever. The gains have helped prop up subdued domestic spending, but could magnify consumer restraint in a sustained stock slide, economists say.

Write to Jason Douglas at jason.douglas@wsj.com

data.title: No Homes to Rent, No Way to Evict: Inside Spain's Housing Crisis — WSJ
data.description:
By Margherita Stancati, Marcos Garcia Rey and Drew Hinshaw | Photography by Michael Robinson Chávez for WSJ

MADRID — In the spring of 2024, Sonia Moreira told her tenant of over a decade that she planned to sell her property, a top-floor, redbrick apartment in a working-class area outside the Spanish capital.

The tenant, Helizabet Delgado, refused to leave and stopped paying rent. Unemployed and facing health issues, she has benefited from housing laws designed to protect vulnerable tenants from eviction.

Moreira and her husband, meanwhile, have continued making monthly mortgage payments, straining their fragile finances. They hired an antisquatter security firm to pressure Delgado out.

"We can barely make ends meet ourselves. We're vulnerable too," said Moreira, a call-center operator whose husband is a welder. They have a disabled son. "I understand that there is a lack of housing. But why do we, the owners, have to deal with this and pay the cost?"

Tenant and landlady agree on one thing: Both consider themselves victims of one of the world's most broken housing markets.

Housing has become a top concern for people across Europe and the U.S., where living costs are rising fast and new construction isn't keeping pace. Nowhere has the issue become as severe, or as politically explosive, as it has in Spain.

Property prices rose 80% in the decade through 2025, according to Spain's National Statistics Institute. Wages grew just 30%. Spanish households now spend an average of 50% of their income on rent, a figure that climbs to 70% in Madrid and Barcelona. Similar pressures have been building in European cities from Berlin to Prague, Lisbon and Amsterdam.

This weekend, Spain's government may become Europe's first to fall because of housing costs. Recent mass protests over housing prompted leftist Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez to call snap elections, scheduled for Sunday.

Housing has dominated the election campaign, with Sánchez calling it "the great challenge of our time" in a televised debate with conservative People's Party leader Alberto Núñez Feijóo, whose party is narrowly ahead in opinion polls.

Spain faces a classic supply-and-demand problem: Immigration, tourism and the shift toward smaller households have outpaced the creation of homes in urban areas.

Since the 2008 financial crisis burst the real-estate bubble, new construction has became more costly and regulated, with building permits often taking many years to obtain. Successive governments — left and right — gave priority to protecting people from losing their homes.

Sánchez doubled down earlier this month, passing measures that automatically extended leases expiring before 2028 and prolonged an eviction ban.

That did little to address the severe housing shortage. It reflects a broader European doom loop, where rising costs push governments to pass tenant-protection laws that in turn discourage construction and owners from renting out their properties.

Both Sánchez and Feijóo promised to quickly build more homes if elected, with Feijóo calling for construction deregulation. The conservative party's likely coalition partner, the hard-right Vox party, has blamed the crisis on a surge of migrant arrivals and the government's embrace of foreign workers: About a fifth of Spain's 50 million people were born abroad, largely in Latin America. But it will take many years, likely more than one term, to close the housing shortfall, which Spain's central bank last year estimated at 750,000 units.

Barcelona is another case in point. The city draws everyone from European digital nomads and American tourists to a swell of working-class North African immigrants — everyone except developers. The city of two million grew by 29,102 people in 2025 alone, but added just 1,434 homes, according to the Barcelona Metropolitan Housing Observatory, a research group. That is a 20-to-1 ratio of newcomers to new apartments.

As a result, most rental listings never even appear online. The last time Barcelona-based real-estate firm Forcadell listed an apartment on its website was in August. "We posted it at 9 a.m. and by 1 p.m. we had to take it down because we had already received 184 requests to visit it," said Álex Vázquez, a company director.

Real-estate agents juggle waiting lists stretching to hundreds of applicants vying for a single apartment, often accompanied by unsolicited documents: desperate letters of introduction, copies of their tax returns and even photos from their latest family vacations.

"People used to give you specific details about what they wanted: a three-bedroom apartment overlooking Carrer de Tarragona, or a place in Gràcia with two bathrooms. Not anymore. Now they just say, 'Please find me a two-bedroom apartment anywhere in the city of Barcelona,'" said Vázquez.

Given a choice, landlords favor highly paid foreigners over locals, while many have opted to sell rather than risk having a tenant they cannot remove.

Increasing public housing is a priority. Hemmed in by mountains and the Mediterranean shore, Barcelona is difficult to build up by nature. Developers say local laws aren't helping either. Firms building or renovating a project of 600 square meters or more must devote a third of their floor plans to low-income "social housing." The result is that builders aren't constructing much housing, social or otherwise.

Barcelona's local government has stepped in to regulate the market in other ways. In 2024, it introduced rent caps in "stressed" areas where average rent exceeds 30% of household income. About 90% of residents of the wider Catalonia region now live in "stressed" areas. Barcelona became the first major city to ban short-term rentals, a move taking effect in 2028 that should free up some 10,000 homes. Critics say the uncertainty from the changes means far more homes than that will simply never be built.

"Here is where all the most radical housing experiments are being trialed and tested to destruction," said Mark Stücklin, the owner of the Barcelona-based research portal Spanish Property Insight. "It's a laboratory for well-intentioned bad ideas."

Barcelona's left-wing mayor, Jaume Collboni, acknowledged that the changing rules have unsettled owners and developers, but saw the disruption as temporary. "The change in the 'rules of the game' has been very profound — very radical, if you will — and that this entails a period of transition," he said in an interview. "The objective is to move away from the use of housing as a financial asset and instead to ensure it meets the right of people to housing."

Delgado moved into the apartment in Torrejón de Ardoz, outside Madrid, in June 2010. She was once on friendly terms with her landlords, Moreira and her husband, Miguel Aragoneses. After Delgado's ex-boyfriend moved out, the couple agreed to lower her rent to 500 euros a month, or just under $550, according to court documents.

When they ended her lease, Delgado tried buying the property, but the price was too high and an agreement was never reached. The landlords hired a firm — Brigada Desokupa — to pressure her to leave. Employees would show up and bang at the door. Rattled and scared to leave the apartment, Delgado said she abandoned her pet-grooming business.

After more than a decade, and having spent money to fix up the rundown place, Delgado considers the apartment her own. A Spanish court in June ruled in favor of the landlords, but Delgado's eviction was halted after the government introduced new emergency housing measures.

Delgado says it is a matter of time before she must leave. The problem is that she has nowhere else to go.

"I have paid hundreds of thousands of euros in rent over the years. And what do I have to show for it? Nothing," said Delgado. Her only option? "Living in my car. I'll pack up my stuff, put it in storage. That is my plan now."

Write to Margherita Stancati at margherita.stancati@wsj.com and Drew Hinshaw at drew.hinshaw@wsj.com

data.title: Four in five developers in Southeast Asia and India now work under AI usage limits, Agoda report finds
data.description:
As AI agents move into production, organizations are treating AI as a governed and measured business resource

SINGAPORE, Nov. 27, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- A year after developers across Southeast Asia and India were largely writing their own rules for AI, organizations are now stepping in to govern it, according to new findings from Agoda's AI Developer Report 2026. As AI agents move from experimentation into production, companies are treating AI less as an open tool and more as a managed business resource, with usage limits, guidelines, and cost controls.

The shift shows most in how access to AI is managed. Four in five developers now work under some form of usage limit, including token quotas, usage caps, or budget restrictions. These controls scale with organizational size, from 41% of developers at small organizations (1 to 50 employees) to more than 91% at organizations with over 1,000 employees. The report finds these limits are as much a governance tool as a cost mechanism, shaping how and where AI is used across the organization.

Formal guidance is also associated with stronger adoption. Developers at organizations with established AI guidelines report production or broad agent use at 56%, compared with 43% at organizations without them, and codebase readiness at 40%, compared with 30%.

Managing risk has become a leadership priority. Nearly a third of respondents (31%) identify managing AI risk as engineering leadership's biggest challenge over the next 12 months, ahead of integrating AI into workflows (21%) and upskilling existing talent (18%). Engineering leaders surveyed for the report note that policy alone is not enough. Some argue the larger gap is literacy rather than policy: decision-makers need to understand what they are deploying well enough to know what governance it requires. In regulated environments, the challenge is more structural, as legal or regulatory requirements may restrict how sensitive data can be used with external AI services.

Idan Zalzberg, Chief Technology Officer at Agoda, said: "Last year, developers across the region were building their own guardrails for AI. This year, organizations are catching up. As AI agents take on more of the work, AI becomes something companies have to manage like any other business resource, with visibility into who uses it, what it costs, and whether the output can be trusted. The goal of governance is not to slow developers down. It is to let them use AI at scale, safely."

At Agoda, this approach is built into the company's engineering infrastructure. Its GenAI Proxy serves as a unified layer that authenticates usage, enforces limits, monitors costs, and supports compliance across multiple model providers. Because switching between models is straightforward, teams can evaluate them offline and on live traffic, matching each task to the most suitable model, from frontier models for complex work to smaller, lower-cost models for routine tasks.

The Agoda AI Developer Report 2026 was commissioned by Agoda and conducted in partnership with Macramé Consulting. It surveyed over 800 software developers and engineering leaders across India, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand, and Vietnam, and includes insights from regional companies such as Omise, SCB 10X, and dataxet. It examines how developers are navigating the shift from AI assistants to autonomous AI agents.

For more information and to download the free report, visit Agoda AI Developer Report 2026.

SOURCE Agoda

data.title: Rupee rally faces oil test; inflows, positive sentiment provide cushion
data.description:
The Indian rupee's recent rally faces a fresh test from rising oil prices, though sustained foreign inflows and positive sentiment towards local assets are expected to help cushion the currency.

The rupee is expected to open largely flat, having settled at 92.4450 to the dollar on Thursday. The South Asian unit is up 2.6% this month, the top-performing currency in Asia.

Brent crude pushed past the $96 level on reviving concerns about supply disruptions. A series of events this week has increased the Middle East risk premium, pushing oil prices higher.

Meanwhile, foreign investors continue to pile into Indian equities amid uncertainty over the sustainability of returns from AI-related investments, providing support to the rupee.

Foreign investors bought more than $600 million worth of Indian shares on Thursday, according to preliminary data, taking November inflows to $16 billion. The buying spree has now wiped off about half of the outflows posted in the first 10 months of the year.

Sentiment towards Indian assets has undergone a marked reassessment in recent weeks, driven largely by a retreat from the AI trade.

The rupee's rally, returning foreign inflows and the Reserve Bank of India's willingness to let the currency appreciate are all contributing to a change in overall market perception, a currency trader at a bank said.

That change is visible in the options market, where betting on a rupee rally now costs more than positioning for a decline, pointing to a change in the currency's prospects, the trader said.

Asian cues

Asian cues were largely subdued, with most regional currencies trading in narrow ranges. Asian equities were mostly higher alongside US equity futures.

The rupee has shown a weaker correlation with its regional peers in recent sessions, reflecting expectations that any further pressure on AI-linked markets could accelerate the rotation of funds towards Indian assets and boost the rupee.

The rupee's recent strength stands in contrast to the dollar index, which is hovering at a 22-month high.

data.title: China warns of retaliation after Trump administration proposes new tariffs over overcapacity
data.description:
The new round of tariff tug-of-war appears to have escalated, as China warned Thursday that it could take “necessary measures” in response to Washington’s newly announced tariffs, which could unsettle the fragile trade-war truce between the two countries ahead of its January 10 expiration.

NECESSARY MEASURES 

When Washington announced proposed tariffs on a range of countries on Wednesday, it set China’s rate at 20%, while cautioning that it could rise to 40%.

As per an AFP report, Chinese commerce ministry spokesman He Yadong said that China has urged the United States to correct its 'erroneous practices' and also urged it to return to resolving issues through dialogue and consultation.

He Yadong added, "China will closely monitor developments and reserves the right to take necessary measures to firmly defend its legitimate rights and interests."

The exchange of these statements adds to the worry of a repeat of the back-and-forth trade war between China and the US post-Trump Liberation-Day tariff, which saw Trump impose new tariffs on Chinese imports, triggering retaliatory measures that escalated until some duties reached 145%.

The trade truce agreed by Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping in October 2025 was extended by two months in September, through January 10.

TRUMP NEW TARIFF WAR 

US President Donald Trump has for years criticised China’s enormous trade surplus with the United States, arguing that it has weakened domestic manufacturing and cost American jobs.

The Trump administration, which has been bruised by the midterm elections, reignited tariff uncertainty when the United States said that it is preparing to raise tariffs on India, China, and several other major trading partners, citing alleged industrial subsidies and excess manufacturing capacity.

US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer is expected to release the findings of an investigation initiated on March 11 under Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974. The inquiry covers 16 economies, including India, China, the European Union, Japan, South Korea, Vietnam, and Bangladesh.

According to ChainCatcher citing Reuters, Tokyo's core consumer price index rose 2.9% year over year in November, up from 2.6% in October and below the market median forecast of 3.0%. The index includes fuel prices but excludes fresh food. Its increase was the fastest since July 2025 and the highest in 16 months, keeping inflation above the Bank of Japan's 2% target for a third consecutive month.

An index excluding both fresh food and fuel rose 2.5% year over year in November, down from 2.6% in October. The increase in prices partly reflected the end of government utility subsidies, while food, daily necessities and hotel costs also rose.

Tokyo prices are viewed as a leading indicator of national trends and will be among the factors considered by the Bank of Japan at its two-day policy meeting ending December 18. After raising rates in June, the central bank raised its policy rate to 1.25% in September, then held it steady in October and said underlying inflation was broadly at its 2% target. A majority of analysts in a Reuters survey expected a rate hike in December and another by the end of March next year.

data.title: Gold rises as rebound in tech stocks offsets rate-hike concerns
data.description:
Gold rose as a tentative recovery in technology stocks and a weaker US dollar offset the prospect of interest-rate hikes by the Federal Reserve.

Bullion climbed as much as 1.7% to near $3,627 an ounce, on track for a weekly gain after rebounding from a 15-month low two days ago. Asian stocks advanced for a second day, extending a rally following weeks of volatility in the artificial intelligence trade, while a gauge of the dollar fell 0.1%, making bullion priced in the US currency cheaper for most buyers.

Sentiment remains fragile, however, at the end of a choppy week of trading. The yellow metal has remained below $4,000 an ounce since Nov. 11 as traders gauged the Fed’s path for combating sticky inflation. It’s still on track for a third monthly loss of more than 6%, extending a fall from a record high in January that gained pace after the US-Iran war sent energy costs soaring.

The Fed’s preferred measure of underlying inflation for October, released Wednesday, reinforced expectations that the central bank will tighten policy when it meets in December. Higher borrowing costs are typically negative for gold, which doesn’t pay interest. The market is also weighing the likelihood of further rate hikes early next year if price pressures continue.

“Gold faces a critical support zone between $3,450 and $3,500, the area from which prices broke out in August 2025 before staging their historic rally to record highs,” said Hebe Chen, senior market analyst at Vantage Global Prime. “This is now the line in the sand for gold — holding above this zone could provide a foundation for stabilization, while a decisive break below would raise the risk of a deeper correction.”

Spot gold climbed 1.4% to $3,616.36 an ounce at 10:24 a.m. in Singapore. Silver surged 3.6% to $43.04 an ounce. Platinum and palladium also advanced.

data.title: Asian gasoline margin flips to negative
data.description:
By Mohi Narayan

Asian gasoline margins flipped into negative territory on Thursday amid expectations of higher supplies and lower demand, while a rally in crude oil benchmarks also pressured the crack, traders and analysts said.

The refining profit, or crack, (GL92-SIN-CRK) for gasoline shrank to minus $5.92 per barrel over Brent crude, the lowest level since April 2020, from a record peak of $50.53 on October 1.

Gasoline crack spreads usually shrink heading into the northern hemisphere's winter, when fuel demand falls. However, this year they hit record highs on a tight supply outlook, caused by the Middle East war, Russia's export ban and lower inventories at key trading hubs.

The margins fell to three-year lows last week and have been on a downward trend since late October amid hopes of higher Chinese and Gulf supplies.

Meanwhile, inventories at key trading hubs also rose last week, adding pressure to the cracks.

Singapore's light distillate stocks, including naphtha and gasoline, climbed to an over one-month high of 11.51 million barrels in the week to November 25, government data showed.

Gasoline imports into the city-state climbed to 310,000 tons (2.2 million barrels) from 67,000 tons in the prior week, while exports rose about 24% on-week to roughly 567,000 tons. South Korea was the top supplier at about 109,000 tons, followed by Japan at 49,000 tons.

U.S. gasoline stocks (USOILG=ECI) rose by 1.7 million barrels last week to 217.7 million barrels.

data.title: Indonesia bourse sanctions five companies over free-float share data discrepancies
data.description:
The Indonesia Stock Exchange said on Friday that it had sanctioned five listed companies for failing to accurately report free-float share ownership data and for not correcting the discrepancies by the prescribed deadline.

  • The bourse did not specify what the sanctions were

  • One company sanctioned by the bourse is PT MNC Tourism Indonesia , formerly known as MNC Land, a tourism company behind the Lido tourism project affiliated with US President Donald Trump

  • MNC Tourism Indonesia did not immediately respond to a request for comment

  • The bourse said it identified discrepancies in the calculation and reporting of free-float shares by several listed companies and subsequently directed them to verify their disclosures and submit corrective filings by a specified deadline

  • The sanctions follow broader market reforms implemented by Indonesian authorities after global index provider MSCI warned that it could downgrade the $1.4 trillion economy to "standalone" status

  • Indonesian authorities have spent much of the year trying to address MSCI's concerns, tightening disclosure requirements and laying out plans to raise minimum free floats

  • Free-floating shares are those openly available for public trading and not held by large core holders such as company officials, long-term investors, or government bodies

data.title: South Korean shares rise more than 2% on hopes of policy support
data.description:
Key points:
  • KOSPI rises, foreigners net buyers
  • Korean won strengthens against dollar
  • South Korea benchmark bond yield rises

Round-up of South Korean financial markets:

** South Korean shares rose more than 2% on Friday as hopes of market-stabilising measures supported dip-buying around 10-month lows, although the benchmark index was still set for a second consecutive weekly loss.

** The benchmark KOSPI was up 104.57 points, or 2.25%, at 4,817.04 as of 0220 GMT, after rising 0.3% in the previous session.

** The index is still down 1% this week after dropping 8% last week.

** Earlier this week, the KOSPI slumped to a 10-month low on persistent worries about a slowdown in the global AI investment boom, prompting policymakers to consider deploying market stabilisation funds.

** "The rebound could be limited until there actually are fresh inflows from stabilisation funds, but there is no need to take an even more pessimistic approach at this point," said Han Ji-young, an analyst at Kiwoom Securities.

** "We believe that the Securities Market Stabilization Fund could be revised up to 20-40 trillion won, versus the current 10.76 trillion won ($8.01 billion)," Citi economist Kim Jin-wook said, expecting the fund to be utilised as early as next month.

** South Korea's finance minister, Lee Hyoung-il, again vowed on Friday to remain prepared to take necessary measures depending on market conditions.

** Chipmaker Samsung Electronics rose 1.93%, while peer SK Hynix gained 1.71%.

** Among other index heavyweights, battery maker LG Energy Solution climbed 3.15%, while Hyundai Motor and sister automaker Kia Corp were up 2.90% and 0.96%, respectively.

** Of the total 906 traded issues, 734 shares advanced, while 148 declined.

** Foreigners were net buyers of shares worth 290.5 billion won.

** The won was quoted at 1,343.0 per dollar on the onshore settlement platform , 0.07% higher than its previous close at 1,343.9.

** The most liquid three-year Korean treasury bond yield (KR3YT=RR) rose by 1.9 basis points to 3.645%, while the benchmark 10-year yield rose by 2.7 basis points to 3.803%.

($1 = 1,343.4800 won)

data.title: Rupee rally faces oil test; inflows, positive sentiment provide cushion
data.description:
By Nimesh Vora

The Indian rupee's recent rally faces a fresh test from rising oil prices, though sustained foreign inflows and positive sentiment towards local assets are expected to help cushion the currency.

The rupee is expected to open largely flat, having settled at 92.4450 to the dollar on Thursday. The South Asian unit is up 2.6% this month, the top-performing currency in Asia.

Brent crude pushed past the $96 level on reviving concerns about supply disruptions. A series of events this week has increased the Middle East risk premium, pushing oil prices higher.

Meanwhile, foreign investors continue to pile into Indian equities amid uncertainty over the sustainability of returns from AI-related investments, providing support to the rupee.

Foreign investors bought more than $600 million worth of Indian shares on Thursday, according to preliminary data, taking November inflows to $16 billion. The buying spree has now wiped off about half of the outflows posted in the first 10 months of the year.

Sentiment towards Indian assets has undergone a marked reassessment in recent weeks, driven largely by a retreat from the AI trade.

The rupee's rally, returning foreign inflows and the Reserve Bank of India's willingness to let the currency appreciate are all contributing to a change in overall market perception, a currency trader at a bank said.

That change is visible in the options market, where betting on a rupee rally now costs more than positioning for a decline, pointing to a change in the currency's prospects, the trader said.

ASIAN CUES

Asian cues were largely subdued, with most regional currencies trading in narrow ranges. Asian equities were mostly higher alongside US equity futures.

The rupee has shown a weaker correlation with its regional peers in recent sessions, reflecting expectations that any further pressure on AI-linked markets could accelerate the rotation of funds towards Indian assets and boost the rupee.

The rupee's recent strength stands in contrast to the dollar index, which is hovering at a 22-month high.

data.title: Iron Ore Prices Fall as Supply Growth, Weakening Demand Weigh — Market Talk
data.description: Iron ore is lower in early Asia trade, with prices weighed as supply growth and weakening demand persist, says Xingye Futures analysts in a note. data.title: Copper Higher Supported by Strong AI Spending Expectations — Market Talk
data.description: Copper is higher in early Asian trading. Prices are supported by strong near-term AI spending expectations, according to ANZ research analysts in a commentary. Copper is a key metal for data center development. Spending on data centres and other AI-related infrastructure is likely to remain strong in the next few quarters, the analysts say. They noted that the Bank of Korea lifted its policy rates after upgrading its GDP forecasts for 2027, in part due to the strong tailwinds from the AI boom. data.title: Elevated oil, fresh debt supply may pressure Indian bonds
data.description:
By Dharamraj Dhutia

Indian government bonds could face further selling pressure in early trading on Friday as traders brace for fresh debt supply through a weekly auction, while elevated oil prices could influence the central bank’s policy decision next week.

The benchmark 6.94% 2036 bond (IN069436G=CC) yield is expected to move between 7.21% and 7.27%, according to a private bank trader. It ended at 7.2365% on Thursday, posting its biggest single-session rise since October 12.

New Delhi is due to raise 330 billion rupees ($3.57 billion) through a bond sale later in the day, including the liquid 7-year paper.

"Benchmark yield should consolidate around 7.25% until the auction, and further trajectory would be guided by the cutoffs," the trader said.

Brent crude remained above $96 per barrel during Asian trading as the latest escalation in the Middle East revived concerns about supply disruptions.

Higher oil prices pose risks for India, a major crude importer, as they could widen the current-account deficit, weaken the rupee and fuel inflation.

Sentiment also soured after the Reserve Bank of India said food-price pressures remained broad-based and data pointed to a "higher generalisation of price pressures."

The comments appeared in the central bank’s monthly bulletin after retail inflation breached the RBI’s upper tolerance limit of 6% in October.

Investors are now awaiting the RBI's December 4 policy decision. A majority of economists polled by Reuters expect a 25-basis-point rate increase, although some see scope for a larger move.

RATES

Overnight index swap rates are likely to trade with an upside bias, after rising sharply in the previous session.

On Thursday, the 1-year (INR1YMIBROIS=CC) rate ended 7.75 bps higher at 6.52%, while the 2-year rate (INR2YIBROIS=CC) jumped 6.5 bps to 6.4550% and the liquid 5-year rate (INR5YMIBROIS=CC) rose 7.5 bps to 6.4575%.

($1 = 92.4450 Indian rupees)

data.title: Binance lifts withdrawal suspension after $6.3 billion crypto heist
data.description:
Binance said on Thursday its withdrawal recovery work is complete, and it has lifted its withdrawal suspension after a record $6.3 billion was stolen in a hack last month.

The crypto platform added that a small number of networks are temporarily paused while they undergo maintenance or planned upgrades, separate from its completed recovery work.

The FBI had said on November 12 that it had seized more than $1.2 billion of cryptocurrency reported stolen last month from Binance, the world's largest crypto exchange.

The theft of about $6.3 billion from Binance is regarded as the biggest crypto heist in history, and the FBI has previously attributed it to a North Korean hacking group known as TraderTraitor.

The total stolen amounts to around a sixth of North Korea's estimated gross domestic product, which shows how significant the haul could be for the country.

North Korea had however denied any involvement in the hack.

The US government and private sector have so far combined to freeze more than $2.7 billion of the stolen funds, and the Justice Department said earlier this month that it has now obtained court authorisation to seize or restrain more than $1.2 billion of that total.

The $6.3 billion was stolen on October 29, and about $2.85 billion of the tokens were frozen by their issuers, but the rest remains in circulation. Because tokens in circulation can be swapped and moved quickly, each day of delay makes tracing and freezing harder.

Crypto researchers told Reuters that money launderers working for North Korea have stepped up the movement of funds through THORChain and coinjoin in recent days, a sign the two services have become cogs in a complex money-laundering operation involving tens of thousands of transactions across different blockchains and crypto services.

data.title: Asian Currencies Might Be Weighed by AI Uncertainties — Market Talk
data.description: Asian currencies could be weighed down by artificial intelligence uncertainties, DBS Group Research's Chang Wei Liang says in commentary. A major U.S. AI chipmaker has reportedly halted all shipments of servers with its chips to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia, he notes. "There are no other non-U.S. commercial alternatives for such AI chips," he says, adding that the move will have a major impact on Asean data center investments. The Malaysian ringgit and Thai baht are likely to further weaken if foreign direct investment into data centers slows markedly, he says. The U.S. dollar is flat at 4.1130 ringgit and little changed at 34.03 baht, LSEG data shows.(amanda.lee@wsj.com)
